I’m retaining a broad shortlist of repeat offenders, small-float/high-OI names, recent sharp movers, and new listings; historical hit rates favor relapse setups, but prior large onsets also justify checking seemingly calm names. I’ll distinguish actual asset removals from trading-pair removals before treating announcements as evidence of constrained arbitrage.

The final ranking favors contracts with a history of sustained, deep episodes rather than merely a high chance of touching −0.10%. I checked 96-hour paths for 64 candidates and episode histories for 30; all 15 selections also pass the explicit quiet screen.

Probabilities remain below 40%, anchored to historical quiet-coin base rates. Borrow constraints are inferred from liquidity and positioning—not confirmed borrow availability—and pair-removal notices are not treated as whole-asset delistings. ZAMA and SENT were reviewed but excluded because the available evidence does not establish a launch/settlement catalyst in the target week.
